proposals.before: Five years, scholars no false records, mourning periods not commanded yet orderly.
proposals.after: Five years, the shi had no conscription registers; mourning periods were orderly without being commanded.
proposals.reason: 尺籍 are military conscription registers, not 'false records'; 士 here are men of service, not 'scholars'.

proposals.before: Wen Gong said: 'Son then self consider have crime, sha ren also have crime?'
proposals.after: Wen Gong said: 'Son then self consider have crime, gua ren also have crime?'
proposals.reason: 寡人 is misrendered as the nonsensical 'sha ren'; it is the ruler's self-reference.

proposals.before: Gong yizi see good cloth yet family woman expel.
proposals.after: Gongyi zi see good cloth yet family woman expel.
proposals.reason: 公儀子 should be rendered as Gongyi zi (Master Gongyi), not the broken 'Gong yizi'.

decisions.reason: Focus unit 士無尺籍 contrasts with the prior literal’s “scholars no false records”: 尺籍 are military conscription registers, and 士 here are men of service, not scholars. The proposed literal restores that sense; 喪期不令而治 is already rightly “mourning periods … orderly without being commanded.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 士無尺籍，喪期不令而治

decisions.reason: Duke Wen’s speech has 寡人亦有罪邪, the ruler’s self-reference 寡人 (gua ren), not “sha ren.” Replacing the nonsensical romanization corrects a real mistranslation without changing the rest of the literal.
公儀子 is the honorific for Gongyi Xiu (compound surname 公儀 + 子); splitting it as “Gong yizi” is wrong. “Gongyi zi” restores the correct name segmentation while leaving the rest of the literal intact.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 公儀子見好布而家婦逐
